[element-string-date]
=== `<string-date>` Date as a String

Date represented as text.

#### Usage/Remarks
This element allows dates within the citation elements to be free-form or all text, not constrained by the STS <<element-date,`<date>`>> model.
*Best Practice* While the <<element-string-date,`<string-date>`>> element may be used for any date that is represented as a sequence of characters (i.e., “January, 2001”, “Fall 2001”, “March 11, 2001”), it is best practice, when possible, to tag the year, month, and/or day as numbers, so “January, 2001” would become:
[source,xml]
....
...
<ref id="B12">
 <label>[12 Lapeyre]</label>
 <element-citation>
  <string-name>Rene Lapeyre du Fontclaire Carnu, IV</string-name>
  <article-title>Foraminifera of the Lower Hellstooth</article-title>
  <source>Local Paleo</source>
  <string-date iso-8601-date="1924-03">
   <month>March</month>, <year>1924</year></string-date>
  <publisher-loc>Rockville, MD</publisher-loc>
 </element-citation>
</ref>
...
....

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>>, <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>>, <<element-related-article,`<related-article>`>>, <<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>>
#### Description

Any combination of: Text, numbers, or special characters <<element-day,`<day>`>> <<element-day,Day (in a citation)>> <<element-era,`<era>`>> <<element-era,Era (in a citation)>> <<element-month,`<month>`>> <<element-month,Month (in a citation)>> <<element-season,`<season>`>> <<element-season,Season (in a citation)>> <<element-year,`<year>`>> <<element-year,Year>>
